title: The physical columns of rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case are not in any source
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 11 and 13; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15
description: The TSD P7 T3.1 defines decision_log_entry (DF-DEC-001 to 031) and approval (DF-DEC-032 to 053) field by field and names the four rule tables only as tables of the module, with no field list, no state column, no artifact column and no type. The legacy story names the fields of a version in section 11 by BR Field IDs (DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-299) and fixes the load, the state list and the Blob reference, but gives no physical column, type or nullability, so the migration, the unique key and the index of the 00:01 read cannot be written from the sources.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 has no subsection for rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row or rule_test_case; legacy section 11 lists DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-299 by name only and legacy section 13 states 'No new table and no migration: V072_1 of RWB-E1-072 created rule_package, rule_package_version and the four columns'.
owner_role: TechX and the P7 solution architect
proposed: Take the column names, types and nullability from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary at implementation on the field names the legacy story fixes, and confirm the artifact columns with the embedded Drools kit of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON.

title: No provided operation of the case service returns the open case facts a dry run needs
source: Ownership Map v1, P3 provided operations; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11; legacy RWB-E1-073 section 11; FSD P7 A2.7
description: The dry run evaluates a draft against every open case and counts the cases whose result would change by product, queue and rule, which needs the product group, queue, region, exposure band and deviation flag of the open book (DF-CAS-003, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-012, DF-CAS-015, DF-CAS-019). The legacy read this through the P3 repository in process; in the target the facts belong to rwb-case and cross one REST hop, and no source names the operation, its filters or its paging.
evidence: Legacy section 11 closes 'the case fields are read only through the P3 repository for the dry run'; legacy section 13 lists 'RuleDryRun ... reads case fields through the P3 repository'; the TSD P7 T-A.1 lists eight P7 endpoints and no case-fact read; the FSD P7 A2.7 names the rules component as the integration point only.
proposed: Add the paged open-case fact read to the rwb-case contract and to its row of the API Specification, filtered by status and paged, and have the dry run use it under RWB-P3-E1073-CON with the 2 s one-hop timeout.

title: Which owned event announces a rule package version in force is not stated
source: TSD P7 T5.3; Ownership Map v1, P7 events EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30; Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-14
description: P7 owns three events (EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30) and the TSD P7 T5.3 names two published events, DecisionRecorded and ApprovalRequested, neither of which is a rule-package promotion. The owning services have to learn that a version is in force, and no source states which event identifier carries that announcement, what it is called under the naming rule, or what its payload holds.
evidence: TSD P7 T5.3 lists DecisionRecorded (Published) and ApprovalRequested (Published) only; the Ownership Map gives P7 EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 with no name; legacy section 13 has the effective-date job move the state with no event.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the event catalogue owner
proposed: Name the announcement rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 on rwb.decision.events.v1 keyed by the package code, carrying the package code, the version label, the in-force time and the SHA-256, and map it to the free identifier of EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog.

title: The value of rules.testcases.min is assumed and no parameter catalogue holds it
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3, 8 and 13; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06; FSD P7 A2.7
description: The legacy story requires at least rules.testcases.min scenarios on a load, states the value as 50 and marks it assumed, and names the value as a row of the parameter catalogue owned by the case module. In the target the parameter is read through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06) and no source gives a parameter code or a confirmed value, so the guard, its default and its test data rest on an assumed 50.
evidence: Legacy section 3 reads 'rules.testcases.min = 50 (assumed)'; legacy BR10 reads 'at least rules.testcases.min scenarios (50, assumed)'; the FSD P7 A2.7 fixes 50 test cases in its examples and names no parameter.
owner_role: P3 parameter owner and the P7 business analyst
proposed: Register rules.testcases.min with the value 50 in the parameter catalogue of rwb-case and confirm it with RW-COE at the first package load; the guard reads the parameter and no value is written in code either way.

title: The legacy endpoints and their controller sit in the access module, while the Ownership Map gives them to P7
source: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 12 and 13; Ownership Map v1, P7 and P4 rows; Template and Rules R3 and R5.5 DP-13
description: The legacy story labels its five operations '(P4 endpoint)' and puts the controller in the access module package recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages while the checks sit in recovery.casewf.rules, which fits a modular monolith. The Ownership Map attributes the same five operations plus the package list to P7, and the target keeps one deployable service per module with its own schema and login. The story follows the Ownership Map and places the whole path in rwb-decision, and records the difference.
evidence: Legacy section 12 heads each endpoint 'POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions (P4 endpoint)'; legacy section 13 reads 'endpoints and the package version writes in the P4 package recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages'; the Ownership Map lists /admin/rule-packages, /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, the approve, rollback and dry-run operations under P7.
owner_role: P7 solution architect and the Ownership Map owner
proposed: Keep the operations and their authority checks in rwb-decision as the Ownership Map has them, and record the move from the access module in the Change Register; the rights themselves stay rows of the rwb-access role model.
